subject: Post-call: SwiftPay savings scenarios & budget ask
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <emorales@swiftpay.com>, SwiftPay Procurement <procurement@swiftpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: SwiftPay savings scenarios & budget ask

Hi Elena / SwiftPay team,

Thanks again for the call today — concise recap below and a couple of asks so we can size a firm pilot proposal.

TL;DR (numbers are early estimates):
- Current reported token volume: ~1.2B tokens/month (prod).
- Current effective unit cost (your reported blended rate): ~$0.000012/token -> ~ $14.4k/month baseline.
- Levers we think will materially reduce spend: batching (continuous request bundling), prefix/KV caching, model variant + quantization, and routing decisions (mixed-hosted/dedicated).
- Realistic savings band for a 4–6 week pilot: 35%–55% depending on tolerance for model/latency tradeoffs. That implies post-pilot run-rate between ~$6.5k–$9.4k/month (illustrative).

Pain points you confirmed:
- Peak latency spikes causing degraded UX at high concurrency (95th P90 spikes >300ms; target is <=200ms 95th).
- Token spend volatility drives budgeting headaches for Product and Finance.
- Procurement requires a clear pilot budget and SOC2 evidence before legal approval.

Goals from the call:
1) Demonstrate 30%+ unit-cost reduction at parity or acceptable latency tradeoffs.
2) Prove reliability at your peak traffic window (daily 100k concurrent inference ops).
3) Produce a clear run-rate and rollback plan for production rollout.

What we propose next (asks for you):
- Confirm the monthly token range (min/typical/max) and a 7‑day peak sample window so we can size batching and cache savings precisely.
- Confirm firm SLO target (you mentioned 200ms 95th).
- Budget guardrail for pilot: do you have an upper limit for a 4–6 week engagement? Elena, you mentioned Finance is looking for a 6–8k/month commitment earlier in the call — please confirm.
- Procurement timeline: target decision date and any required PO or MSA milestones.

What we'll deliver in our pilot proposal (attachments referenced):
- A side-by-side scenario model (attached: batching-savings-model.xlsx) with conservative/typical/aggressive assumptions.
- A one-page pilot scope + price (attached: SwiftPay_Pilot_Scope_and_Pricing_v1.pdf).
- SOC2 cert link and short security appendix.

Quick, realistic numbers we will formalize:
- Batching: expect 18%–28% CPU/GPU token cost reduction depending on request size distribution and acceptable additional 25–75ms aggregation latency.
- KV/prefix caching for repeated prompts: 8%–15% savings on token infra if there are repeat prefixes (your metrics team said ~22% repeat rate for common flows).
- Quantization/model variant: 15%–30% savings depending on top‑level LLM choice (we’ll propose 1-2 variants that keep your latency SLO).
- Combined: 35%–55% typical on pilot if all levers combine cleanly; we’ll run a conservative waterfall in the spreadsheet.

Next steps I recommend from Redwood side:
1) You send the 7‑day peak sample + confirmation of pilot budget guardrail.
2) We return a final two-option pilot price (hosted-focused + dedicated-minimal-commit) and an ops checklist within 48 hours.
3) If acceptable, Procurement pulls PO/MSA and we schedule a kickoff the following week.

I'll wait for the token samples and budget confirmation. If useful I can attach an explicit 6‑week SOW and two pricing options in the follow-up email.

Best,
Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Solutions (Redwood Inference)
---
Attachments: SwiftPay_Pilot_Scope_and_Pricing_v1.pdf (1 page), batching-savings-model.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Elena Morales <emorales@swiftpay.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: SwiftPay savings scenarios & budget ask

Rafael — thanks for the quick recap and the model you mentioned. A few clarifications from Procurement / Finance:

- Pilot budget: Finance has tentatively greenlit a $8k/month cap for a short, tightly-scoped pilot (4–6 weeks). If you can do a clean hosted-first option under that, we should be able to move quickly.
- Payback requirement: Execs want a payback < 3 months when projecting to production.
- Security: Procurement will need SOC2 and a short addendum on data retention (we retain logs for 90 days, need to understand Redwood's retention and support for deletion requests).
- Timeline: our internal procurement sprint aims to sign pilots by the week of 2026-09-13. Legal will need a customer-friendly MSA or a short-term addendum.

Please put together two clear pricing options (hosted + batching vs small dedicated commit) and call out the guaranteed savings assumptions. Also attach the SOC2 link.

—Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Product Ops, SwiftPay
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Post-call: SwiftPay savings scenarios & budget ask (internal)

Raf — quick internal:
- Put two clear options in the follow-up:
  * Option A (hosted-first + batching/caching opt): fixed pilot fee $7,500/mo for 6 weeks, includes 2 engineer-days for integration and standard SOC2 appendix.
  * Option B (small dedicated pool): $9,500/mo with a 3‑month minimum reserved capacity; includes 1 week of dedicated infra setup and KMS option.
- Ben, please attach the SOC2 link and the short retention statement.
- Emphasize the payback calc (we need a <3mo narrative) with an appendix showing break-even at 35% savings.

Keep it short and put the spreadsheet in the send.

Marissa
Director, Customer Success (Redwood Inference)
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <emorales@swiftpay.com>, SwiftPay Procurement <procurement@swiftpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-31T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: SwiftPay pilot proposal + mutual action plan (proposal + attachments)

Elena / Procurement — thanks again. Attached are the two-option pilot proposal and the scenario model. Short summary and MAP below.

What we're sending (attached):
- SwiftPay_Pilot_Scope_and_Pricing_v1.pdf (2 pages): Option A (hosted-first) at $7,500/mo for a 6-week pilot; Option B (small dedicated) at $9,500/mo with a 3-month minimum.
- batching-savings-model.xlsx: conservative / typical / aggressive worksheets with token volume inputs, batching compression assumptions, cache hit rates, and resulting monthly spend.
- SOC2.pdf link (Ben cc'd) and a short retention appendix.

Mutual Action Plan (MAP) — proposed cadence and owners:
1) SwiftPay: confirm the 7-day token sample, and confirm budget cap (Procurement) — due by 2026-09-03 (owner: Elena).
2) Redwood: return final SOW and DocuSign-ready MSA/addendum — due by 2026-09-06 (owner: Rafael).
3) SwiftPay Legal/Procurement: review and return PO or redlines — target complete by 2026-09-13.
4) Kickoff: target week of 2026-09-20 (engineering onboarding, test data, and monitoring hooks).

Key callouts on numbers (from the attached model):
- Baseline: 1.2B tokens/mo = $14.4k/mo (blended).
- Option A (hosted-first + batching/caching): model shows 38% conservative savings -> $8.9k/mo run-rate; aggressive case 48% -> $7.5k/mo.
- Option B (dedicated small pool): faster inference tail, slightly higher fixed cost but can hit 45% savings earlier due to pinned resources.

If those options look good I can send a DocuSign MSA + SOW link (pre-filled) when you confirm the budget cap and the sample token window.

Regards,
Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Solutions (Redwood Inference)
